releaseEvidence: 37a99cba: Update to new waveform generation algorithm.
90cbc7a3: Add support for sending voice note waveforms.

implementationEvidence.testEvidenceNote: Focused tests cover the new PCM-to-decibel generator, exact storage and render bar counts, unsigned resampling, sender-provided validation and duration clamping, audio-only upload dependencies, oversized incoming waveform rejection, and attachment persistence fixtures.

baseFailureEvidence: The v8.28.4 generator stores 46 bars using peak-relative normalization; the final generator stores 100 bars using the released decibel/noise-bed algorithm while keeping rendering at 46 bars.
The v8.28.4 upload graph runs compression directly into upload and does not gate audio uploads on GenerateAudioWaveFormJob.
The v8.28.4 service attachment schema and transform omit audioWaveform and audioDurationSeconds, so outgoing and incoming attachment pointers cannot carry the released metadata.
The v8.28.4 envelope validator does not reject an otherwise valid attachment pointer for an oversized waveform.
The v8.28.4 stored waveform record has no senderProvided origin flag, its renderer exposes the stored bar count directly, and a no-URI attachment cannot render a stored sender waveform.
The v8.28.4 backup FilePointer has no audio waveform or duration fields, so sender waveform metadata cannot survive export and restore.

boundaryAudit.baseIsAncestorReason: The local source mirror is a shallow partial clone and does not contain enough intermediate graph objects for an independent ancestry proof.
boundaryAudit.verification: Local read-only tag, commit, tree, and patch queries establish exact object IDs and the semantic base/final delta; full-history ancestry remains a scored-calibration preflight.

longHorizonSignals: The capability crosses media decoding, waveform math, database serialization, job dependency ordering, outgoing transport, incoming validation, renderer adaptation, and backup conversion.
The two focused commits change 52 file entries in total and add unit, envelope-validation, upload-graph, database, and backup-fixture coverage.
The canonical graph contains independent invalid-remote, held-upload, stale-cache, interrupted-generation, and no-local-media recovery paths.
